touches.text: The ticket IS its own manager. It carries its workflow and status, and asks each gate whether it can transit. If refused, it gets itself back to design for fixing. If no handler is available to ask, it throws a trouble and waits until we decide. Design is CC and Akien. Akien, 2026-11-11, Q#85: "you and me. later there will be a specific agent for it, but that's so far off we're not even thinking about it now except 'after the outline is implemented'." So until then a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, which both of us read when a session opens, and nothing posts to a design verb that no machine answers.

Commit often. WHY: so we never wind up with stray files or incomplete work. [Q#94: A crossing into PROVEME refuses while anything in either tree is uncommitted (working_tree_clean, widened by ticket c1cca2e3dc23 on your 8w, F11 and 8x; unclaimed dirt refuses too, 8u). So with peers on one box, one peer's ticket records (another ticket's log/state, the artifact journal) block every other peer's crossing. Measured 2026-11-12: 3195b3b834bc's PROVEME was refused twice on the Dell, over d692ef650534's records and then the orchestrator's. Do records that artifact.locate claims for ANOTHER ticket stop blocking (unclaimed dirt and any code dirt still refuse), or does the whole-tree rule stand and peers serialise their crossings per box?]

More than one builder runs at a time, so work is kept apart by branches: each ticket's work on its own branch, named by the ticket id, merged locally with git, no pull request (GitHub is hosting only). WHY: "the best way to manage scaling is branches."
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.

Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.

The chart chain machines (9.3.2): orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate, verdict. [Q#98: The verdict's instrument run, and the proofs that exercise it, need bubblewrap, which Windows does not have, so `cairn test --exec` refuses there ("the instance seal is not confirmed ... bubblewrap (bwrap) is not installed") and three teeth stay red on Windows: test_the_instrument_is_run (two teeth) and the standing-verdict-proofs-stay-green check. Measured 2026-11-13. Whether Windows gets its own seal is the per-OS seal question in Q#90 (9.4.2.3.3); this one is the narrow choice that stands beside it: until that is settled, do the bwrap teeth skip on Windows (and read as not-run there), or do they stay red until Windows has a seal of its own?]
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
